facts.text: Townsville's Museum of Tropical Queensland showcases relics from HMS Pandora and displays Great Barrier Reef life.
The town’s library on the James Cook University Douglas campus bears the name of Indigenous land rights icon Eddie Mabo.
The historic waterfront along Ross Creek preserves original wharves and early port buildings, a reminder of Townsville's maritime roots.
Aboriginal groups such as the Wulgurukaba, Bindal, Girrugubba, Warakamai and Nawagi were the first peoples of the Townsville area.
The Strand, a long tropical beach and garden strip, runs along Townsville’s coast and is a favorite spot for locals and visitors alike.
Magnetic Island, just off Townsville’s coast, is largely a national park and a popular destination for snorkeling and wildlife spotting.
